name: Prospektor
//tagline: #216, 25 Aug 2026. One string, five rendered uses: the <title> suffix (base.njk, via the metaTitle budget), the JSON-LD WebSite description, the footer, the og:image:alt default, and the article OG cards baked by tools/og.js. Previously "Your AI pre-sales team" — #168 found presales is an occupied category (solution engineering: Vivun, Consensus, Navattic; a G2 category and a job title), so the site was miscategorising itself in the structured data of all 42 pages. The replacement is benefit-framed rather than descriptive, on the operator's own redirect, and drops "outreach" in favour of warm introductions and deliverables. Keep it SHORT: the metaTitle budget is 60 characters and drops the suffix rather than truncating it, so length decides reach — 18 chars keeps the suffix on 16 of 42 pages where 33 chars kept 6 and 22 kept 11. #450, 31 Aug 2026: "Your AI GTM engine" became "Leads that fit you". GTM is the same jargon that made two non-sales readers unable to say what the product does, and it sat in the ONE string a stranger meets before the site does — the <title> suffix, which is what a search result shows. The replacement is the operator's own framing ("prospektor finds you leads tailored to you") and is 18 characters, exactly what it replaced, so it keeps the suffix on the identical 17 of 45 pages — measured against the built titles, not assumed. Re-run tools/og.js after any change here: the article cards bake this string.
//googleSiteVerification: Only needed if Search Console is verified by HTML tag instead of DNS TXT. The recommended route is a DNS TXT record at Spaceship, which needs no deploy, survives a hosting change, and verifies a Domain property covering www. and studio. as well — see RUNBOOK-search-console.md. Paste the raw token here (the content= value, not the whole tag) only if DNS is not an option.
description: Teach Prospektor what you're after — customers, partners, resellers, investors — and it finds the companies, names who to contact, and writes what you send.
//nav: #153, 24 Aug 2026. Every item is a real page. Three of the five used to be same-page anchors (/#what, /#how, /#pricing), so the header taught nothing and every click landed on the document you were already reading — the operator's words: "the header is not concise/ good anymore now". The first two are named after the two questions the product answers (CLAUDE.md, The product thesis: WHOM to approach, WHAT to send) rather than after themselves, so the nav carries the positioning instead of restating the word "it" twice. The homepage keeps its #what/#how/#pricing ids — deep links from elsewhere still land.
//description: Fallback <meta name=description> and the WebSite node's description. Every page carries its own now (#137) so this is a last resort, but it is still the one a new page inherits before anyone writes it one — so it stays inside the 160 characters a search result shows.
